strengths: Meaning 2's plate (a waterfall carving through rock) is a literal, well-chosen match for "Like water: fill it, flow on."
The drop at 14.4 s lands exactly on the question-to-screen-1 cut, where the energy table jumps from 4 to 7 — the biggest visual move (zoom + shake) sits on the biggest music move.
Hook is plain, recognizable, and readable in one glance, with hard white-on-black contrast.
End card holds long enough (5.4 s, typing on then full text + URL) and the credit reads clearly at 1.8 s, matching the series' held-card convention.

changes.change: On screens 3 and 4 (YOUR DAY, READ / ASK · CAST · REFLECT), the glitch-styled title text sits directly on top of live app copy ("Good evening, 蕴斋", "THE HEXAGRAM", "each position means. These rules guide...") instead of a clear background band. Give the titles a solid or gradient scrim, or crop the capture so the title has empty app-chrome behind it, the way screens 1-2 sit cleanly over the bird/castle art.
changes.why: The RGB-split title glyphs overlapping live sentence text make both unreadable at a glance, which is the one thing the showcase section needs to prove — that a viewer can tell what the app does.

changes.change: Put the question line on a dark scrim or box like meaning 1 and meaning 2 use, instead of leaving it bare over the matrix code-rain background.
changes.why: Right after two plate-backed meaning lines, dropping to bare code-rain for the question is a legibility and continuity step down — the white text is readable but the frame reads thinner than the two before it.

changes.change: Swap meaning 1's plate (a figure walking through a dust/sand storm) for something water- or abyss-themed, matching meaning 2's waterfall and the hexagram's actual image.
changes.why: The current plate fits "keep moving" but not "The Abyss" — a viewer sees a desert scene under a water hexagram, which weakens the visual read of the hexagram itself.

changes.change: Give screen 4 a clear visual anchor (art or a UI element) instead of leaving it text-only against the same input-box screenshot; it is the last screen before the end card and currently reads as the weakest of the four.
changes.why: Screens 1-2 pair the app name with strong art (bird, castle); screen 4 ends the showcase on plain UI chrome, which is a weaker note to hand off into the end card.

review.notes: Cannot hear the track, so whip-cut placement against actual beat transients (not just per-bar energy) is unverified — worth a sound-on check that the whip-up/whip-left/whip-right sequence through meaning 1 -> meaning 2 -> question actually lands on beats and not just within the right bar. Also worth checking on a phone screen whether the code-rain characters behind the question text (visible in still 07) read as noise at small size.
